gaps.sentence: The reason ___ he resigned was never explained.
gaps.explanation: 'The reason why' is the fixed pattern.

gaps.sentence: The programme ___ I watched last night was about volcanoes.
gaps.explanation: 'Which' refers to things, even when it is the object of the clause.

gaps.sentence: Mr Okafor, ___ the whole department respects, is retiring in May.
gaps.explanation: Formal non-defining clause with a person as object: whom.

gaps.sentence: The man ___ wallet I found works at the post office.
gaps.explanation: 'Whose wallet' means 'the man's wallet'; 'who's' means 'who is' and cannot precede a noun.

gaps.sentence: The restaurant ___ we had dinner last night has excellent reviews.
gaps.explanation: 'Where' replaces 'in which' after place nouns; no preposition appears in the clause.

gaps.sentence: The Eiffel Tower, ___ attracts millions of visitors, was completed in 1889.
gaps.explanation: For things in non-defining clauses use 'which'; 'that' is not allowed after a comma.

gaps.sentence: My laptop, ___ I bought only last year, has already crashed twice.
gaps.explanation: Non-defining clause about a thing: 'which', never 'that'.

gaps.sentence: That's the office ___ I worked for ten years.
gaps.explanation: 'Where' means 'in which'; 'I worked the office' shows the place role of the gap.
